entities.name: PMID:25433917
observations: Study of Rhododendron ferrugineum, a long-lived mass-flowering shrub, across 28 natural patches.
Sparse patches showed greater selfing/reproductive assurance, but estimated mean lifetime inbreeding depression was approximately 0.90.
Authors concluded that poor lifetime fitness of selfed progeny counteracts the reproductive-assurance benefit of selfing.

entities.name: Rhododendron ferrugineum
observations: Mass-flowering woody perennial shrub studied for selfing, pollination, and lifetime inbreeding depression.

entities.name: Lifetime inbreeding depression ~0.90
observations: Across natural patches, lifetime inbreeding depression was estimated at approximately 0.90, implying selfed lifetime fitness near 10% of outcrossed fitness under the conventional definition.

entities.name: Sparse-patch reproductive assurance
observations: Open seed set declined with floral display, while pollinator-mediated seed set from emasculated flowers was unrelated to floral display; this supports reproductive assurance through selfing in sparse patches.
Mean fruit set was 94.5% across 28 patches and increased with floral display.
